# Scaling Experimentation with Self-Service Metrics
Date: 2026-11-25 | Duration: 35.560001373291016m

## Summary
The discussion focused on improving an experimentation process currently limited by manual, engineering-led testing, feature-flag work, cross-functional dependencies, and limited visibility. Data engineers define metrics, engineers assess feasibility, and weekly coordination contributes to a capacity of three monthly tests versus a target of twenty, while ideas accumulate in a backlog. Self-service experimentation aims to reuse recurring metrics, reduce data-team requests, and increase engineering independence. Optimization centers on revenue per user, platform time spent, website actions, and bets, while Microsoft BI dashboards create interpretation challenges. A proposed governance model lets PMs define metrics, keeps data-team validation, and creates reusable official metrics. GrowthBook supports warehouse-native A/B testing, multi-arm bandits, audience targeting, Bayesian results, goal and secondary metrics, and guardrails. AI capabilities include MCP-assisted experiment creation, metric definitions, analysis, and idea generation. Product analytics and improved discovery-led demos were also discussed.

## Keywords
Experimentation, Feature flags, Warehouse-native analytics, A/B testing, AI experiment workflows, Product metrics
